title: Close gf2-core GF(p^n) extension-field SOTA gaps
description:
Successor epic to `97bf0879` (Close gf2-core SOTA performance gaps). Extends the SOTA closure programme to GF(p^n) extension fields for odd primes p and degrees n > 1, the field family that the parent epic explicitly scoped out per its [hard] criterion 5 ("GF(2), GF(p), GF(2^m), dense factorization/solve, characteristic/minimal polynomial, and sparse matrix-vector/matrix-matrix surfaces each have a final scorecard section"). ## Background The project's stated vision (`CLAUDE.md` § Vision) is "competing with specialized computer algebra systems (Magma/Sage)" for finite-field linear algebra. Magma/Sage cover all GF(p^n); the SOTA closure epic 97bf0879 covers only GF(2), GF(p), and GF(2^m). GF(p^n) for odd prime p and n > 1 is a genuine scope-loss surfaced during 97bf0879's Wave 4 review (see `dev/plans/sota_target_matrix.md` § 3.2 — taxonomy explicitly enumerates only GF(2), GF(p), GF(2^m)). Current implementation state in `crates/gf2-core/src/gfpn/`: * `ExtConfig` trait (`ext_config.rs:62`) — pluggable base field + irreducible extension polynomial. * `QuadraticExt` (`quadratic.rs:229`) — degree-2 tower extensions over arbitrary `BaseField`. * `CubicExt` (`cubic.rs:250`) — degree-3. * `BatchExtField` (`batch.rs:179`) — batched ext-field arithmetic over the same trait. Lean4 proofs at `proofs/Gf2Core/Proofs/` cover `Fp

` plus `QuadraticExt` and `CubicExt`. Maximum supported extension degree is **3**; arbitrary degree n is not implemented. Reference-library landscape for GF(p^n) (none evaluated by 97bf0879's Wave 2): * **NTL 11.6.0 `mat_GF2E`** is currently used canonical for `matmul × GF(2^32)` per `b13799ac`. NTL's `ZZ_pE` / `mat_ZZ_pE` covers GF(p^n) for odd p — same library, different module. * **FLINT 3.5.0 `fq_nmod_mat`** covers GF(p^n) for arbitrary p and n; not harnessed in `benchmarks/reference/flint_bench.c`. * **LinBox 1.7.1 `GivaroExtension<...>`** covers extension fields generically; the Wave-2 `linbox_promotion_evidence.md` § *Coverage scope* explicitly excludes extension-field cells. * **Magma / Sage** — out-of-scope correctness oracles per the parent epic's posture; same applies here unless a future user-approved amendment promotes a specific reproducible benchmark. This is a **placeholder epic**. Detailed breakdown into stories and tasks is deferred until 97bf0879 closes and a dedicated breakdown session runs. ## Success Criteria - [hard] The SOTA target matrix (`dev/plans/sota_target_matrix.md`) § 3.2 is amended to include GF(p^n) as a fourth field family with a representative-prime-and-degree taxonomy (e.g., GF(7^2), GF(7^3), GF(31^2), GF(p^n) for at least one large prime + degree). - [hard] At least one external reference library is promoted to canonical for `matmul × GF(p^n)` under the existing acceptance protocol (`dev/plans/sota_reference_acceptance_protocol.md` § 3 five-criterion checklist). Candidate set: NTL `mat_ZZ_pE`, FLINT `fq_nmod_mat`, LinBox `GivaroExtension`. Rejected candidates carry an exclusion note per protocol § 9. - [hard] gf2-core's GF(p^n) implementation surface is extended beyond the current degree-3 cap. The minimum new coverage is determined by the breakdown phase but must include at least quartic extensions (degree 4) and a path to arbitrary degree n via either a `QuarticExt` / `QuinticExt` chain or a generic `Ext` tower that does not require a per-degree module. - [hard] Every in-scope `(operation, GF(p^n))` cell of the extended target matrix is within 1.5x of the canonical reference or carries an explicit user-approved scope amendment (mirrors the 97bf0879 1.5x contract). - [hard] The dense surface (`fgemm`, `pluq`, `echelon`, `invert`, `solve`, `charpoly`, `minpoly`) and the sparse surface (`spmv`, `sparse-matmul`, `sparse×dense`, `sparse-elim`) each carry a final scorecard section over GF(p^n) with raw numbers and ratio-to-reference. Cells without an external reference candidate carry a `no-independent-oracle` exclusion analogous to the GF(2^m) non-matmul cluster in 97bf0879. - [hard] No `unsafe` leaks outside `gf2-kernels-simd` / `gf2-kernels-hip`; high-level `gf2-core` remains safe. - [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, and `doc-review` pass on every child issue and on the epic closure. - [hard] Lean4 proof coverage is extended to the new GF(p^n) implementation surface where the existing `proofs/Gf2Core/Proofs/` infrastructure permits (Aeneas / Charon round-trip on the new modules), or an explicit non-goal note records the verification gap. - [hard] A final presentation attached to the epic summarizes achieved ratios across GF(p^n), reference-promotion outcomes, and remaining non-goal boundaries (mirrors the 97bf0879 closure deck). ## Notes This epic groups three implementation work-streams identifiable at placeholder time. Detailed decomposition will turn each into a dedicated story during the breakdown phase: 1. **Algorithmic work-stream.** Quartic and higher-degree extensions (or a generic `Ext` tower); polynomial modular reduction over odd characteristic; Frobenius / norm / trace operations; charpoly/minpoly over the base field. Reuses the `ExtConfig` trait pattern from `gfpn/ext_config.rs`. 2. **Reference-lane work-stream.** Mirrors the 97bf0879 Wave-2 reference-evaluation pattern: each candidate library (NTL `ZZ_pE`, FLINT `fq_nmod_mat`, LinBox `GivaroExtension`) is evaluated under the existing acceptance protocol; promotion-evidence docs land at `dev/plans/_gfpn_promotion_evidence.md`. The protocol document itself does **not** need amendment; § 7's allowed-fields list already permits GF(p^n) by virtue of being templated on field-family rather than enumerated. 3. **Matrix-amendment work-stream.** Extends `dev/plans/sota_target_matrix.md` § 3.2 (taxonomy), § 4 (library roster), § 5 (matrix tables — adds operation-rows over GF(p^n)), § 6 (exclusion ledger if any cells carry no oracle), § 7 (consumption guide for downstream optimization stories), and § 9 (success-criteria mapping). Per the protocol § 12 maintenance template, this is an amendment, not a rewrite. The dependency edge to 97bf0879 enforces ordering: this epic stays in `backlog` until 97bf0879 closes. A breakdown session is not scheduled at placeholder-creation time; the user can invoke `/jit-breakdown` against this issue once 97bf0879 has closed and the user is ready to begin GF(p^n) work. GPU acceleration is optional and follows the same posture as 97bf0879: only wire HIP/ROCm work when the CPU target matrix shows a gap that cannot plausibly close on CPU.
